did_you_know.text: The psalm opens with a repeated call to give the Lord glory and strength. The expression “sons of gods” addresses powerful beings or heavenly beings, and the central idea is that even the mighty are called to recognize the Lord’s supremacy.
In the opening verses, the word “ascribe” appears three times. This repetition emphasizes the call to give the Lord glory, acknowledge the holiness of his name, and bow down before him.
The voice of the Lord is described as sounding over the mighty waters. This description connects the divine voice with storms, thunder, and the forces of nature.
The verse joins “strength” with “splendor”: the voice of the Lord is not only powerful but also expresses glory, majesty, and greatness.
The cedars of Lebanon, known as symbols of great and strong trees, are portrayed as breaking before the voice of the Lord. This emphasizes the Lord’s supremacy even over the forces of nature.
Lebanon and Sirion are described as leaping like a calf and a young wild ox. This vivid, living image emphasizes the trembling and shaking of the mountains.

The expression “he cuts out flames of fire” describes the voice of the Lord as something that carves out or produces flames. In the context of the storm, the image recalls the power of lightning and fire in nature.
The voice of the Lord also shakes the wilderness, especially the wilderness of Kadesh. The psalm presents the Lord’s power as extending from the waters and mountains to the vast wilderness.

In the same sequence in which the voice shakes nature, it is also described as causing the does to give birth and stripping the forests bare. The image includes both a storm and the process of birth, emphasizing the voice’s all-encompassing power.
After describing the flood and the storm, the Lord is portrayed as a king seated forever. The contrast between the raging waters and his steadfast rule emphasizes his eternal kingship.
The psalm ends with a twofold promise: the Lord gives strength to his people and blesses them with peace. Thus, the movement from storm to blessing connects power with calm and serenity.
